blogs.title: Forgetting to Breathe: Ondine's Curse and the Voluntary-Automatic Breathing Divide
blogs.description: This post explores the fascinating physiology behind central hypoventilation in Chiari malformation—specifically how brainstem compression can selectively spare voluntary breathing while devastating automatic respiratory control. We'll discuss why patients can breathe normally when they think about it but 'forget to breathe' when distracted or asleep, and why the absence of dyspnea despite profound hypoxemia should be a red flag for brainstem pathology.

blogs.title: When the Scope is Normal: A Neurogenic Approach to Unexplained Dysphagia
blogs.description: This post examines the diagnostic approach to dysphagia when standard ENT and GI workups come back negative. We'll discuss the key distinction between mechanical dysphagia (typically worse with solids) and neurogenic dysphagia (equal difficulty with all consistencies), and why persistent choking episodes without structural findings should prompt neurological investigation—including consideration of Chiari malformation as an underrecognized cause of oropharyngeal dysfunction.

blogs.title: Look Again: The Crowded Foramen Magnum Hiding in Plain Sight
blogs.description: This post focuses on the critical lesson of personally reviewing prior imaging rather than relying solely on radiology reports. We'll demonstrate how a CT scan reported as 'normal' 14 years earlier actually showed clear evidence of a crowded foramen magnum—a finding that could have shortened a 14-year diagnostic odyssey. Practical tips for clinicians on what to look for at the craniocervical junction and why this easy-to-miss sign matters.

blogs.title: Beyond AHI: Why Central Apnea Matters More Than You Think
blogs.description: This post discusses the limitations of standard sleep study metrics in capturing clinically significant central hypoventilation. We'll explore why a 'mild' AHI of 6.0 can coexist with dangerous desaturations to 70-80%, the importance of distinguishing central from obstructive events, and how type III sleep studies may underestimate true disease severity. A call to think beyond the numbers when evaluating sleep-disordered breathing in neurological conditions.

blogs.title: The Vertex Allodynia Enigma: Scalp Hypersensitivity in Chiari Malformation
blogs.description: This post explores the unusual symptom of vertex allodynia—where even the weight of the patient's hair caused pain—and its potential relationship to Chiari malformation. We'll discuss the spectrum of occipital neuralgia, 'burning vertex syndrome,' and how cranial nerve and upper cervical nerve involvement in CMI may manifest as cutaneous hypersensitivity. An interesting clinical observation that deserves more systematic study.
